To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
plasma electrolytic oxidation of titanium is a simple method for improving the surface bioactivity of titanium, which is important for its use in orthopedic and dental implants.

plasma electrolytic oxidation can form calcium phosphate-containing coatings with improved corrosion resistance on titanium, which increases the biocompatibility of this material in comparison with bare titanium.

the bioactive PEO-coating formed on titanium by plasma electrolytic oxidation has the following properties: a composition containing calcium phosphate, elastoplastic properties, low friction coefficient, increased wettability, and decreased corrosion rate.

the study of the properties and structure of coatings formed by plasma electrolytic oxidation on commercially pure titanium.
a study of the composition and electrochemical properties of coatings on titanium formed by plasma electrolytic oxidation.
the development and characterization of a new bioactive PEO-coating for commercially pure titanium.
